docs.title: Guidot
docs.text:
Real-time time-series graph widget for Godot 4.

Guidot lets you drop a single node into any Godot scene and get a fully interactive, live-updating plot — no boilerplate required.

  • :material-chart-line:{ .lg .middle } Real-time plotting

    Push data from anywhere in your scene tree and watch it appear on the graph instantly.

  • :material-axis-arrow:{ .lg .middle } Multiple Y-axes

    Up to 6 left and 6 right Y-axes, each independently scaled and colour-coded.

  • :material-window-maximize:{ .lg .middle } Sliding window & fixed mode

    Follow the latest data automatically, or lock the view to a specific time range.

  • :material-gesture-tap:{ .lg .middle } Fully interactive

    Scroll to zoom, Ctrl+drag to pan, double-click to set exact limits — all at runtime.

docs.title: Quick look
docs.text:
YourScene
├── Guidot_Time_Series_Graph   ← add this node
├── Guidot_Data_Server         ← one per scene
└── YourNode
    └── Guidot_Data_Source     ← push data here

A Guidot_Data_Source collects data channels and forwards them to the Guidot_Data_Server. The graph subscribes to whichever channels you select via the in-game wizard.

docs.title: Version
docs.text: Field Value Plugin version 0.1.0 Godot version 4.x License MIT

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Godot 4.x
  • No external dependencies

docs.title: 1. Copy the addon
docs.text:
Copy the addons/guidot/ folder into your project's addons/ directory:

your_project/
└── addons/
    └── guidot/          ← copy this folder
        ├── plugin.cfg
        ├── plugin.gd
        ├── guidot_time_series_canvas.gd
        ├── guidot_time_series_graph.gd
        └── ...

docs.title: 2. Enable the plugin
docs.text:
In the Godot editor:

  1. Open Project → Project Settings
  2. Go to the Plugins tab
  3. Find Guidot in the list and set its status to Enabled

docs.title: 3. Add required nodes to your scene
docs.text:
The minimum scene tree you need:

YourScene (Node or any root)
├── Guidot_Data_Server
├── Guidot_Time_Series_Graph
└── YourDataProducerNode
    └── Guidot_Data_Source

Tip

Guidot_Data_Server auto-discovers all Guidot_Data_Source nodes in the scene tree on _ready. You do not need to wire them together manually.

docs.title: 4. Verify
docs.text: Run the scene. The graph should appear with an empty plot and default axes. Right-click the graph to open the configuration wizard and subscribe to data channels.

docs.title: What is Guidot?
docs.text: Guidot is a Godot 4 plugin that provides an interactive, real-time time-series graph widget. It is designed for games or tools that need to visualise live numeric data — physics values, AI state, network metrics, sensor readings, or any float stream — without leaving the Godot editor or writing custom rendering code.

docs.title: The graph node
docs.text: Guidot_Time_Series_Graph is the top-level node you add to your scene. It owns the canvas, axes, and all UI chrome. You can have multiple independent graphs in the same scene.

docs.title: Server / client architecture
docs.text:
Data flows through a lightweight publish-subscribe system:

Guidot_Data_Source  ──push──▶  Guidot_Data_Server  ──query──▶  Guidot_Time_Series_Graph
Node Role Guidot_Data_Source Lives next to (or inside) the node that produces data. You call add_data_point() on it each frame or whenever a new value is ready. Guidot_Data_Server Central store. Receives data from all clients in the scene tree. The graph queries it every frame. Guidot_Data A named channel descriptor — one per data stream (e.g. "velocity_x", "rpm"). Guidot_Data_Group Optional grouping of related channels shown together in the subscriber UI.

docs.title: Axes
docs.text: Axis Class Notes Time (T) Guidot_T_Axis_Canvas Horizontal axis. Supports Sliding Window (auto-follows latest data) and Fixed (user-locked range). Value (Y) Guidot_Y_Axis_Canvas Vertical axis. Up to 6 left + 6 right independently scaled axes.

docs.title: Key features
docs.text:
• Zero-config startup — add the nodes, push data, done.
  • In-game wizard — configure Y-axes, T-axis range, opacity, and buffer mode without pausing the game.
  • Interactive axes — scroll to zoom, Ctrl+drag to pan, double-click to open the limit editor, single-click a tick label to edit inline.
  • Data grouping — organise related channels so the subscriber UI stays clean.
  • Edit mode — press E to enter edit mode; drag to move the graph, grab corners to resize it.

docs.title: Example: Basic Sine Wave
docs.text: The simplest possible Guidot setup — one channel, one data source, live sine wave.

docs.title: Scene tree
docs.text:
SineWaveDemo (Node)
├── Guidot_Data_Server
├── Guidot_Time_Series_Graph
└── SineProducer (Node)
    ├── Guidot_Data_Source
    └── sine_producer.gd   ← attach this script

docs.title: Script
Running it
docs.text:
1. Run the scene.
  2. Click the gear icon on the graph.
  3. In the Data tab, tick sine.
  4. The graph starts plotting a live sine wave.

Tip

To see more of the wave, open the wizard → T-Axis Setup → set the sliding window to 5 seconds.

docs.title: Example: Data Grouping
docs.text: When you have many channels, Guidot_Data_Group keeps the wizard's subscriber list readable by collecting related channels under a collapsible header.

docs.title: Scene tree
docs.text:
GroupingDemo (Node)
├── Guidot_Data_Server
├── Guidot_Time_Series_Graph
└── VehicleNode (Node)
    ├── Guidot_Data_Source
    └── vehicle_telemetry.gd

docs.title: Script
docs.text:
vehicle_telemetry.gd
extends Node

@onready var _client: Guidot_Data_Source = $Guidot_Data_Source

# Motion channels
var _vel_x: Guidot_Data = Guidot_Data.new()
var _vel_y: Guidot_Data = Guidot_Data.new()
var _accel: Guidot_Data = Guidot_Data.new()

# Engine channels
var _rpm:   Guidot_Data = Guidot_Data.new()
var _temp:  Guidot_Data = Guidot_Data.new()

var _t: float = 0.0

func _ready() -> void:
    # Name every channel
    _vel_x.set_name("velocity_x")
    _vel_y.set_name("velocity_y")
    _accel.set_name("acceleration")
    _rpm.set_name("rpm")
    _temp.set_name("temperature")

    # Group: Motion
    var motion_group: Guidot_Data_Group = Guidot_Data_Group.new()
    motion_group.set_name("Motion")
    motion_group.add_channel(_vel_x)
    motion_group.add_channel(_vel_y)
    motion_group.add_channel(_accel)

    # Group: Engine
    var engine_group: Guidot_Data_Group = Guidot_Data_Group.new()
    engine_group.set_name("Engine")
    engine_group.add_channel(_rpm)
    engine_group.add_channel(_temp)

    _client.register_data_group(motion_group)
    _client.register_data_group(engine_group)
    _client.update_server()

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
    _t += delta

    _client.add_data_point(_vel_x, sin(_t))
    _client.add_data_point(_vel_y, cos(_t))
    _client.add_data_point(_accel, sin(_t * 2.0) * 9.8)
    _client.add_data_point(_rpm,   3000.0 + sin(_t * 0.5) * 1000.0)
    _client.add_data_point(_temp,  90.0   + sin(_t * 0.1) * 10.0)

docs.title: Result in the wizard
docs.text:
The Data tab will show two collapsible sections:

▼ Motion
    ☑ velocity_x
    ☑ velocity_y
    ☑ acceleration
▼ Engine
    ☑ rpm
    ☑ temperature

Tick individual channels or collapse groups you are not interested in to reduce visual noise.

Tip

Channels that are not registered inside any group still appear in the wizard — they show up in an Ungrouped section at the bottom.

docs.title: Script
Assigning channels to axes
docs.text:
By default all subscribed channels share the first Y-axis. To spread them across independent axes:

  1. Open the wizard → Y-Axis Setup → set Left axis count to 2.
  2. In the Data tab, subscribe all three channels.
  3. Assign sine and cosine to Y-Axis 1, and noise to Y-Axis 2.

Each axis can then be zoomed and panned independently.

Note

Channels on different axes are drawn in different colours automatically. The colour is inherited from the axis's display colour.

docs.title: Axis Controls
docs.text: All axis interactions work at runtime without pausing the game.

docs.title: Mouse controls
docs.text: Input Where Effect Scroll up Over any axis Zoom in (narrow range) Scroll down Over any axis Zoom out (widen range) Ctrl + left-drag Over any axis Pan the axis Double-click Over any axis Open the Limit Settings popup Single-click on min/max tick Y or T axis edge labels Open inline editor for that limit Right-click Over any axis Open the axis context menu

docs.title: T-axis modes
docs.text: The time axis has two operating modes toggled from the wizard or via code.

docs.title: Sliding Window (realtime)
docs.text:
The axis automatically advances to follow the newest data point. The visible window width is configurable.

# Set a 30-second rolling window
_t_axis_node.set_window_size_s(30.0)
_t_axis_node.change_graph_mode(Guidot_T_Axis_Canvas.TAxisMode.SLIDING_WINDOW)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
The axis stays locked to the range you set. Any user interaction (inline edit, limit dialog, zoom, pan) automatically switches to Fixed mode.

_t_axis_node.change_graph_mode(Guidot_T_Axis_Canvas.TAxisMode.FIXED)

Info

Opening the Axis Limit Settings from the right-click menu while in Sliding Window mode automatically switches to Fixed. Use the Sliding Window Settings menu item to go back.

docs.title: Limit Settings popup
docs.text:
Double-click any axis to open a small popup where you can type exact min/max values.

  • Min = Max is rejected (zero-span axis causes division by zero in tick spacing).
  • Min > Max is allowed — this flips the axis, rendering the plot upside-down.
  • Press Apply or hit Enter to confirm.

docs.title: Inline editor
docs.text: Single-click the leftmost (min) or rightmost (max) tick label on any axis to edit that limit directly on the axis without opening a popup. Press Enter to apply, Escape to cancel.

docs.title: In-game wizard
docs.text: The wizard is the primary configuration UI. Open it at runtime by clicking the gear icon on the graph.

docs.title: Graph tab
docs.text: Setting Description Opacity Transparency of the whole graph (0 = invisible, 1 = opaque) Graph Mode FIXED — data is buffered to a fixed size. REALTIME — sliding window follows live data.

docs.title: Y-Axis Setup tab
docs.text:
Setting Description Left axis count Number of Y-axes on the left side (1–6) Right axis count Number of Y-axes on the right side (0–6)

Adding or removing axes takes effect immediately. Each channel must be (re-)assigned to an axis after changing the count.

docs.title: T-Axis Setup tab
docs.text: Setting Description Sliding window size (s) Width of the rolling window in seconds when in Realtime mode Fixed min / max Exact time range when in Fixed mode

docs.title: Data tab
docs.text: Lists all registered channels grouped by their Guidot_Data_Group. Tick a channel to subscribe the graph to it. The channel immediately appears (or disappears) on the plot.

docs.title: Programmatic configuration
docs.text:
All wizard settings are also accessible via GDScript on the Guidot_Time_Series_Canvas reference inside the graph node.

@onready var _canvas = $Guidot_Time_Series_Graph._guidot_ts_canvas

# Switch T-axis to realtime with a 15-second window
_canvas._t_axis_node.set_window_size_s(15.0)
_canvas._t_axis_node.change_graph_mode(Guidot_T_Axis_Canvas.TAxisMode.SLIDING_WINDOW)

# Set a fixed Y range on the first axis
var handler = _canvas._y_axis_manager.get_available_axis_handler()[0]
handler.get_axis_node().setup_axis_range(-10.0, 10.0)

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph LR
    A[Your Node<br/>Guidot_Data_Source] -- add_data_point --> B[Guidot_Data_Server]
    B -- query_data_with_channel_name --> C[Guidot_Time_Series_Graph]
    C -- renders --> D[Plot canvas + axes]

Every frame the graph queries the server for buffered data points on all subscribed channels and redraws the plot.

docs.title: Guidot_Data
docs.text:
A lightweight descriptor for one data stream. Create one per signal you want to plot.

var my_channel: Guidot_Data = Guidot_Data.new()
my_channel.set_name("engine_rpm")

docs.title: Guidot_Data_Source
docs.text:
Attach this node to whatever scene node produces data. It auto-discovers the nearest Guidot_Data_Server on _ready.

# Register a channel
_client.register_data_channel(my_channel)
_client.update_server()

# Push a value (call each frame or on event)
_client.add_data_point(my_channel, current_rpm)

Update rate cap: The client is capped at 60 Hz (Godot's default process rate). Calls above 60 Hz are silently clamped.

docs.title: Guidot_Data_Group
docs.text:
Group related channels so the wizard's subscriber list stays organised.

var motion_group: Guidot_Data_Group = Guidot_Data_Group.new()
motion_group.set_name("Motion")
motion_group.add_channel(velocity_x_channel)
motion_group.add_channel(velocity_y_channel)

_client.register_data_group(motion_group)
_client.update_server()

Channels inside a group are shown under a collapsible header in the wizard.

docs.title: Guidot_Data_Server
docs.text: You normally do not call this directly — the client and graph handle it. Place one instance in your scene tree and everything else auto-connects to it.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
_ready()
  └─ Guidot_Data_Source scans for Guidot_Data_Server
  └─ registers itself as a client
  └─ you call register_data_channel / register_data_group
  └─ call update_server() to flush channel registrations

_process()
  └─ call add_data_point() with your values
  └─ server buffers the point
  └─ graph queries server and redraws

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Setting up Guidot takes three steps:

  1. Declare your data channels — create Guidot_Data objects that name each stream.
  2. Push data — call add_data_point() on your Guidot_Data_Source each frame (or on demand).
  3. Subscribe — open the in-game wizard and tick the channels you want to see.

docs.title: Minimal GDScript setup
docs.text:
extends Node

# 1. References to the Guidot nodes (add them in the scene tree)
@onready var _client: Guidot_Data_Source = $Guidot_Data_Source

# 2. Declare a channel
var _speed_channel: Guidot_Data = Guidot_Data.new()

func _ready() -> void:
    _speed_channel.set_name("speed")
    _client.register_data_channel(_speed_channel)
    _client.update_server()   # tell the server about the new channel

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
    var speed: float = calculate_speed()          # your value
    var t: float     = Time.get_ticks_msec() / 1000.0
    _client.add_data_point(_speed_channel, speed)

Note

add_data_point uses the server's internal clock for the timestamp. You do not need to pass t manually unless you want custom timestamps.

docs.title: In-game workflow
docs.text: Action How Open wizard Press the gear icon on the graph, or right-click → Settings Subscribe to a channel Tick the checkbox next to its name in the Data tab Change Y-axis count Wizard → Y-Axis Setup Switch T-axis mode Wizard → T-Axis Setup → choose Realtime or Fixed Adjust opacity Wizard → Graph → Opacity slider Zoom Scroll wheel over an axis Pan Ctrl + left-drag over an axis Set exact limits Double-click an axis to open the limit dialog Edit inline Single-click a min/max tick label Move graph Press E to enter Edit mode, then drag Resize graph Press E, then drag a corner handle
